summary: Mecca sits on the eastern shore of the Salton Sea in the Coachella Valley, where the flat, sun-scorched desert floor stretches toward the Santa Rosa Mountains to the west and the Chocolate Mountains to the east — a landscape so wide-open that the sky dominates every sightline, and annual average daytime highs of 87°F with over ten hours of daily sunshine mean summer temperatures routinely push well past 110°F. This is agricultural country at its most elemental: date palm groves and table grape vineyards define the local economy, and the area's major employers are concentrated in farming, packing, and related logistics rather than office parks or hospitals. At a median household income of roughly $45,000 and a median home value around $222,000, the price-to-income ratio of about 4.9× makes ownership numerically within reach compared to coastal California, though median rent at $900 a month still claims nearly a quarter of gross household income — a tight margin given a poverty rate near 19%. The town itself is small, just under seven square miles, with no real downtown commercial district; grocery runs and sit-down dining generally mean driving into Coachella or Indio. Mecca is a place where the economy is tied directly to the ground beneath it, and daily life is shaped far more by harvest cycles and desert heat than by any urban rhythm.
